result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Full-source/configuration review: security configuration, all application controllers/services/entities, both properties profiles, compose, Dockerfile, Oracle bootstrap scripts, PowerShell provisioning, example environment and documentation. No credential values are included in findings.

Runtime database/admin passwords are required external substitutions rather than hard-coded defaults: application.properties:14, application-docker.properties:5, docker-compose.yml:7,9,34,36, SecurityConfig.java:37 and oracle-init/create-user.sh:11,13. Example-file placeholders are explicitly documented as replacements, not confirmed production credentials.

azure-setup.ps1:15-22 generates passwords with a cryptographic RNG; lines 39,41 allow external values. No hard-coded encryption/signing key was found. Schema grants are limited to the intended application schema; public gallery access is explicit design, not an inferred permission defect.

Limitations: no deployed secret values, actual filesystem/cloud ACLs, authentication-event logs, external audit services or historical commits were inspected. No dependency/CVE rescan. NOT_FOUND is no confirmed pattern in the current production source/configuration, not proof that deployed credentials or permissions are secure.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: SecurityConfig.securityFilterChain lines 46-61 enables HTTP Basic authentication but configures no authentication/security-event audit handler or listener. Production code has no audit event consumer. PhotoServiceImpl.uploadPhoto lines 179-180 and deletePhoto line 212 log security-critical data mutations with photo identifiers/filenames but omit the authenticated principal and request origin/correlation; DetailController.deletePhoto line 69 likewise omits actor identity. Consequently the application does not provide attributable audit records for mutations, and application-level recording of failed authentication is not configured. This is a logging/traceability gap, not evidence that authentication is bypassed. External gateway or separately configured runtime audit logs were not available to verify.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
